propositions: reconcile-bridge-canary.yml contains ~200 lines of untestable, unlintable YAML logic (staleness classification and two alert-ticket state machines) that should be extracted to Python for unit testability and ruff coverage

the four logic families (check-heartbeat, heartbeat-alert, check-binding-drift, binding-drift-alert) have branchy decision logic with API errors, lifecycle transitions, and rebar CLI calls that benefit from extraction and separate unit tests
the two CAS push loops (reconcile-bridge.yml commit-back and canary flush) must remain in YAML verbatim and tested as before, mirroring the test-in-place pattern from ticket 4c4f

the extracted scripts/canary_bridge.py must preserve error handling dispositions: alert-write failures fail loud (non-zero exit), dedup finds degrade gracefully to empty, and rebar bridge-fsck exit-code-1-with-drift-JSON is treated as drift signal not error
DRY_RUN environment gate must be checked at both YAML step-level and inside subcommands as defense-in-depth to prevent unintended rebar mutations
parity between pre- and post-migration workflow_dispatch runs must be operator-attested, confirming identical staleness classification and alert behavior
